title: Baby hip ultrasound
what: The doctor uses ultrasound to check that your baby's hip joints are formed correctly. It is safe and uses no radiation.
why: Usually as a routine check in the first months of life. It matters most after a breech position, if relatives had hip dysplasia, or if the doctor noticed the legs look uneven.
tell_doctor: If your baby was in a breech position
If relatives had hip dysplasia or a dislocated hip
If you noticed uneven skin folds on the legs, or one leg does not spread out as well

prepare.title: Age
prepare.text: The scan is usually done at 1 to 3 months. Your pediatrician or orthopedic doctor will set the timing.

prepare.title: Feeding
prepare.text: Feed your baby 30 to 40 minutes before the visit. A full baby lies more calmly.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Choose clothes that come off easily from the waist down. The diaper stays on, it is just unfastened.

bring: A baby blanket or changing sheet
A pacifier or toy, if your baby likes them
steps: Your baby's lower half is undressed, and your baby is laid on one side
The doctor puts gel on the side of the hip
The probe is held at the joint for a few seconds
Then your baby is turned to the other side, and the second joint is checked
You can stand nearby and hold your baby
feel: It does not hurt your baby. They may not like the cool gel or being held still
after: The gel is wiped off, and you can dress your baby
You usually get the report right away
If the doctor sees a problem, an orthopedic doctor will explain what to do next

faq.q: Why does my baby need a hip ultrasound?
faq.a: To spot hip dysplasia early. In the first months it is easiest to fix, usually without surgery.

faq.q: Is ultrasound harmful for my baby?
faq.a: No. Ultrasound uses no radiation and can be done as many times as needed.

reminders.text: Baby hip ultrasound today. Feed your baby 30 to 40 minutes before the visit. Bring a blanket and a diaper.
